portable.description: Portable ZIP version (no installation, extract only)

default.installScript: TMP=$(mktemp --suffix=.tar.xz) && curl -fL -o "$TMP" 'https://sourceforge.net/projects/doublecmd/files/DC%20for%20Linux%2064%20bit/Double%20Commander%201.1.32/doublecmd-1.1.32.qt6.x86_64.tar.xz/download' && sudo rm -rf /opt/doublecmd && sudo mkdir -p /opt/doublecmd && sudo tar -xJf "$TMP" -C /opt/doublecmd && rm "$TMP" && DC_BIN=$(find /opt/doublecmd -maxdepth 3 -name doublecmd -type f -executable | head -1) && sudo ln -sf "$DC_BIN" /usr/local/bin/doublecmd

default.installScript: TMP=$(mktemp -t doublecmd).dmg && curl -fL -o "$TMP" 'https://sourceforge.net/projects/doublecmd/files/macOS/Double%20Commander%201.1.32/doublecmd-1.1.32.cocoa.x86_64.dmg/download' && MNT=$(hdiutil attach "$TMP" -nobrowse -plist | sed -n 's:.*<string>\(/Volumes/[^<]*\).*:\1:p' | tail -1) && sudo rm -rf '/Applications/Double Commander.app' && sudo cp -R "$MNT/Double Commander.app" /Applications/ && hdiutil detach -quiet "$MNT" && rm "$TMP"

aiPrompts.versionDiscovery: Check Double Commander on SourceForge at https://sourceforge.net/projects/doublecmd/files/ for the latest stable version. Releases are organized in platform-specific folders ('DC for Windows 64 bit', 'DC for Linux 64 bit', 'macOS'), each containing a 'Double Commander {version}' subfolder. Cross-reference with GitHub mirror at https://github.com/doublecmd/doublecmd/releases.
aiPrompts.urlResolution: URL pattern: https://sourceforge.net/projects/doublecmd/files/{platform-folder}/Double%20Commander%20{version}/doublecmd-{version}.{toolkit}.{arch}.{ext}/download. Toolkits: qt6 (modern), qt (Qt5 legacy), gtk2 (Linux only); cocoa (macOS only). Architectures: x86_64, aarch64. Extensions: exe/msi/zip (Windows), tar.xz (Linux), dmg (macOS). Note the trailing /download suffix to bypass the SourceForge file page.
aiPrompts.updateGuidance: Double Commander follows a 1.1.x scheme with frequent patch releases. When bumping the version, update all platform URLs and verify file naming on SourceForge — naming conventions occasionally change (e.g. older 1.1.x releases shipped .deb/.rpm for Linux which were dropped in favor of tar.xz only). The Linux script type is required because the engine's tar.xz extraction is not yet implemented natively; it relies on system tar with xz-utils. The macOS script uses hdiutil because DMG mounting is not implemented in the engine.
